P1● FoundationMCQ · 1 markOriginal

When 4x−7=3x24x - 7 = 3x^24x−7=3x2 is written in standard form, the values of aaa, bbb and ccc are:

standard form ax2+bx+c=0ax^2 + bx + c = 0ax2+bx+c=0; terms change sign when they cross the equals sign (Topic 1). Why it applies: the equation has terms on both sides.

Copies 4x4x4x and −7-7−7 without moving them — but they are on the left, the x2x^2x2 term is on the right.
Subtract 4x4x4x and add 7 on both sides: 0=3x2−4x+70 = 3x^2 - 4x + 70=3x2−4x+7, so a=3a = 3a=3, b=−4b = -4b=−4, c=7c = 7c=7.
Moved the 7 correctly but forgot that 4x4x4x changes sign.
Mixed: a=−3a = -3a=−3 would need b=4b = 4b=4 and c=−7c = -7c=−7 (that is −3x2+4x−7=0-3x^2 + 4x - 7 = 0−3x2+4x−7=0, which is also correct but not offered).

Given: 4x−7=3x24x - 7 = 3x^24x−7=3x2. Asked: aaa, bbb, ccc in standard form.

Concept used: standard form ax2+bx+c=0ax^2 + bx + c = 0ax2+bx+c=0; terms change sign when they cross the equals sign (Topic 1). Why it applies: the equation has terms on both sides.

  1. Reasoning for each option:

    • (a) ✘ Copies 4x4x4x and −7-7−7 without moving them — but they are on the left, the x2x^2x2 term is on the right.
    • (b) ✔ Subtract 4x4x4x and add 7 on both sides: 0=3x2−4x+70 = 3x^2 - 4x + 70=3x2−4x+7, so a=3a = 3a=3, b=−4b = -4b=−4, c=7c = 7c=7.
    • (c) ✘ Moved the 7 correctly but forgot that 4x4x4x changes sign.
    • (d) ✘ Mixed: a=−3a = -3a=−3 would need b=4b = 4b=4 and c=−7c = -7c=−7 (that is −3x2+4x−7=0-3x^2 + 4x - 7 = 0−3x2+4x−7=0, which is also correct but not offered).

  2. Check: 3x2−4x+7=03x^2 - 4x + 7 = 03x2−4x+7=0 rearranges back to 4x−7=3x24x - 7 = 3x^24x−7=3x2 ✔.

  3. Answer (b)

    Common trap: Reading bbb and ccc before writing the standard form — one of the most common mistakes in this chapter.
P2● FoundationMCQ · 1 markOriginal

Which of the following is a quadratic equation?

simplify both sides, then check the highest power (Topic 1). Why it applies: x2x^2x2 or x3x^3x3 terms may cancel.

The x2x^2x2 terms cancel: 2x+5=02x + 5 = 02x+5=0 — linear.
x2−3x=2x+1x^2 - 3x = 2x + 1x2−3x=2x+1 becomes x2−5x−1=0x^2 - 5x - 1 = 0x2−5x−1=0 — quadratic.
Both sides are identical; everything cancels (0=00 = 00=0). It is an identity, not an equation to solve.
The x3x^3x3 terms cancel: −2x−4=0-2x - 4 = 0−2x−4=0 — linear.

Given: four equations. Asked: which is quadratic.

Concept used: simplify both sides, then check the highest power (Topic 1). Why it applies: x2x^2x2 or x3x^3x3 terms may cancel.

  1. Reasoning for each option:

    • (a) ✘ The x2x^2x2 terms cancel: 2x+5=02x + 5 = 02x+5=0 — linear.
    • (b) ✔ x2−3x=2x+1x^2 - 3x = 2x + 1x2−3x=2x+1 becomes x2−5x−1=0x^2 - 5x - 1 = 0x2−5x−1=0 — quadratic.
    • (c) ✘ Both sides are identical; everything cancels (0=00 = 00=0). It is an identity, not an equation to solve.
    • (d) ✘ The x3x^3x3 terms cancel: −2x−4=0-2x - 4 = 0−2x−4=0 — linear.

  2. Check: only (b) keeps an x2x^2x2 term with a non-zero coefficient ✔.

  3. Answer (b)

P3● FoundationVery short answer · 1 markOriginal

Is x=−2x = -2x=−2 a root of 3x2+5x−2=03x^2 + 5x - 2 = 03x2+5x−2=0? Justify.

Full solution

Given: the equation and the value x=−2x = -2x=−2. Asked: whether it is a root.

Concept used: a root makes the equation true when substituted (Topic 3). Why it applies: substitution is the definition of a root.

  1. 1

    Substitute x=−2x = -2x=−2 into the left side.

    3(−2)2+5(−2)−23(-2)^2 + 5(-2) - 23(−2)2+5(−2)−2Swipe to see the whole equation →
  2. 2

    (−2)2=4(-2)^2 = 4(−2)2=4.

    3(4)−10−23(4) - 10 - 23(4)−10−2Swipe to see the whole equation →
  3. 3

    Simplify.

    12−10−2=012 - 10 - 2 = 012−10−2=0Swipe to see the whole equation →
  4. 4

    The left side equals the right side (0).

  5. Check: 3x2+5x−2=(3x−1)(x+2)3x^2 + 5x - 2 = (3x - 1)(x + 2)3x2+5x−2=(3x−1)(x+2), and x+2=0x + 2 = 0x+2=0 at x=−2x = -2x=−2 ✔.

  6. Answer Yes, because 3(−2)2+5(−2)−2=03(-2)^2 + 5(-2) - 2 = 03(−2)2+5(−2)−2=0.

    Common trap: Writing (−2)2=−4(-2)^2 = -4(−2)2=−4, which gives −12−10−2=−24-12 - 10 - 2 = -24−12−10−2=−24 and the wrong verdict.

P4● FoundationShort answer · 2 marksOriginal

Solve x2+3x−28=0x^2 + 3x - 28 = 0x2+3x−28=0 by factorisation.

Full solution

Given: a=1a = 1a=1, b=3b = 3b=3, c=−28c = -28c=−28. Asked: the roots.

Concept used: splitting the middle term; zero-product rule (Topic 3). Why it applies: small integers, standard form.

  1. 1

    Product −28-28−28, sum +3+3+3 → +7+7+7 and −4-4−4.

    x2+7x−4x−28=0x^2 + 7x - 4x - 28 = 0x2+7x−4x−28=0Swipe to see the whole equation →
  2. 2

    Group.

    x(x+7)−4(x+7)=0x(x + 7) - 4(x + 7) = 0x(x+7)−4(x+7)=0Swipe to see the whole equation →
  3. 3

    Factorise.

    (x−4)(x+7)=0(x - 4)(x + 7) = 0(x−4)(x+7)=0Swipe to see the whole equation →
  4. 4

    Zero-product rule.

    x=4orx=−7x = 4 \quad\text{or}\quad x = -7x=4orx=−7Swipe to see the whole equation →

  5. Check: 16+12−28=016 + 12 - 28 = 016+12−28=0 ✔; 49−21−28=049 - 21 - 28 = 049−21−28=0 ✔.

  6. Answer x=4 or x=−7x = 4 \text{ or } x = -7x=4 or x=−7

    Common trap: Splitting as −7x+4x-7x + 4x−7x+4x (sum −3-3−3), which gives (x+4)(x−7)(x + 4)(x - 7)(x+4)(x−7) and the roots −4-4−4 and 777.

P5● FoundationMCQ · 1 markOriginal

The discriminant of 2x2−5x−3=02x^2 - 5x - 3 = 02x2−5x−3=0 is:

D=b2−4acD = b^2 - 4acD=b2−4ac (Topic 5). Why it applies: the definition.

25−2425 - 2425−24: treats ccc as +3+3+3, so −4ac-4ac−4ac comes out negative.
D=(−5)2−4(2)(−3)=25+24=49D = (-5)^2 - 4(2)(-3) = 25 + 24 = 49D=(−5)2−4(2)(−3)=25+24=49.
−25+24-25 + 24−25+24: squares −5-5−5 as −25-25−25.
25+1225 + 1225+12: uses 2ac2ac2ac instead of 4ac4ac4ac.

Given: a=2a = 2a=2, b=−5b = -5b=−5, c=−3c = -3c=−3. Asked: DDD.

Concept used: D=b2−4acD = b^2 - 4acD=b2−4ac (Topic 5). Why it applies: the definition.

  1. Reasoning for each option:

    • (a) ✘ 25−2425 - 2425−24: treats ccc as +3+3+3, so −4ac-4ac−4ac comes out negative.
    • (b) ✔ D=(−5)2−4(2)(−3)=25+24=49D = (-5)^2 - 4(2)(-3) = 25 + 24 = 49D=(−5)2−4(2)(−3)=25+24=49.
    • (c) ✘ −25+24-25 + 24−25+24: squares −5-5−5 as −25-25−25.
    • (d) ✘ 25+1225 + 1225+12: uses 2ac2ac2ac instead of 4ac4ac4ac.

  2. Check: D=49=72D = 49 = 7^2D=49=72, so the roots are rational: (2x+1)(x−3)=0(2x + 1)(x - 3) = 0(2x+1)(x−3)=0 gives −12-\dfrac{1}{2}−21​ and 3 ✔.

  3. Answer (b)

P6● FoundationVery short answer · 1 markOriginal

State the nature of the roots of x2+2x+5=0x^2 + 2x + 5 = 0x2+2x+5=0.

Full solution

Given: a=1a = 1a=1, b=2b = 2b=2, c=5c = 5c=5. Asked: the nature of the roots.

Concept used: the sign of DDD (Topic 5). Why it applies: nature depends only on DDD.

  1. 1

    D=b2−4ac=22−4(1)(5)D = b^2 - 4ac = 2^2 - 4(1)(5)D=b2−4ac=22−4(1)(5).

  2. 2

    D=4−20=−16D = 4 - 20 = -16D=4−20=−16.

  3. 3

    D<0D < 0D<0.

  4. Check: x2+2x+5=(x+1)2+4≥4x^2 + 2x + 5 = (x + 1)^2 + 4 \geq 4x2+2x+5=(x+1)2+4≥4 for every xxx, so it is never 0 ✔.

P7● FoundationMCQ · 1 markOriginal

To factorise 2x2−5x−122x^2 - 5x - 122x2−5x−12 by splitting the middle term, −5x-5x−5x should be written as:

two numbers with product acacac and sum bbb (Topic 2). Why it applies: this is the rule for splitting.

(−8)(3)=−24=ac(-8)(3) = -24 = ac(−8)(3)=−24=ac and −8+3=−5=b-8 + 3 = -5 = b−8+3=−5=b. Then 2x(x−4)+3(x−4)=(2x+3)(x−4)2x(x - 4) + 3(x - 4) = (2x + 3)(x - 4)2x(x−4)+3(x−4)=(2x+3)(x−4).
Product −24-24−24 ✔ but sum +5+5+5: signs swapped.
Sum −5-5−5 ✔ but product −6-6−6, not −24-24−24 — it does not use a×ca \times ca×c.
Sum −5-5−5 ✔ but product +6+6+6; acacac is negative, so the numbers need opposite signs.

Given: a=2a = 2a=2, b=−5b = -5b=−5, c=−12c = -12c=−12. Asked: the correct split.

Concept used: two numbers with product acacac and sum bbb (Topic 2). Why it applies: this is the rule for splitting.

  1. Reasoning for each option:

    • (a) ✔ (−8)(3)=−24=ac(-8)(3) = -24 = ac(−8)(3)=−24=ac and −8+3=−5=b-8 + 3 = -5 = b−8+3=−5=b. Then 2x(x−4)+3(x−4)=(2x+3)(x−4)2x(x - 4) + 3(x - 4) = (2x + 3)(x - 4)2x(x−4)+3(x−4)=(2x+3)(x−4).
    • (b) ✘ Product −24-24−24 ✔ but sum +5+5+5: signs swapped.
    • (c) ✘ Sum −5-5−5 ✔ but product −6-6−6, not −24-24−24 — it does not use a×ca \times ca×c.
    • (d) ✘ Sum −5-5−5 ✔ but product +6+6+6; acacac is negative, so the numbers need opposite signs.

  2. Check: (2x+3)(x−4)=2x2−8x+3x−12=2x2−5x−12(2x + 3)(x - 4) = 2x^2 - 8x + 3x - 12 = 2x^2 - 5x - 12(2x+3)(x−4)=2x2−8x+3x−12=2x2−5x−12 ✔.

  3. Answer (a)

Full solution

Concept used: simplify the surd, then divide every term by the denominator (Topic 2). Why it applies: this is the last step of many formula answers.

    48=16×348 = 16 \times 348=16×3, so 48=43\sqrt{48} = 4\sqrt{3}48​=43​.

    −4±434\dfrac{-4 \pm 4\sqrt{3}}{4}4−4±43​​Swipe to see the whole equation →

    Divide each term on top by 4.

    −1±3-1 \pm \sqrt{3}−1±3​Swipe to see the whole equation →

P9● FoundationShort answer · 2 marksOriginal

The product of two consecutive positive even integers is 168. Form a quadratic equation and find the integers.

Full solution

Given: consecutive positive even integers, product 168. Asked: the equation and the integers.

Concept used: consecutive even integers are xxx and x+2x + 2x+2; word-problem routine (Topic 6). Why it applies: their product gives a quadratic.

  1. 1

    Let the smaller integer be xxx. The next even integer is x+2x + 2x+2.

  2. 2

    Equation:

    x(x+2)=168x(x + 2) = 168x(x+2)=168Swipe to see the whole equation →
  3. 3

    Standard form.

    x2+2x−168=0x^2 + 2x - 168 = 0x2+2x−168=0Swipe to see the whole equation →
  4. 4

    Solve: product −168-168−168, sum 2 → 141414 and −12-12−12.

    (x+14)(x−12)=0(x + 14)(x - 12) = 0(x+14)(x−12)=0Swipe to see the whole equation →
  5. 5

    So x=12x = 12x=12 or x=−14x = -14x=−14.

  6. 6

    Reject x=−14x = -14x=−14: the integers must be positive.

  7. Check: 12×14=16812 \times 14 = 16812×14=168 ✔.

  8. Answer Equation x2+2x−168=0x^2 + 2x - 168 = 0x2+2x−168=0; the integers are 12 and 14.

    Common trap: Using xxx and x+1x + 1x+1 — those are consecutive integers, one of which is odd.

Solve 2x2+5=9x2x^2 + 5 = 9x2x2+5=9x using the quadratic formula.

Full solution

Given: an equation not in standard form. Asked: the roots.

Concept used: standard form first, then the formula (Topic 4). Why it applies: bbb and ccc must be read with correct signs.

  1. 1

    Subtract 9x9x9x from both sides.

    2x2−9x+5=02x^2 - 9x + 5 = 02x2−9x+5=0Swipe to see the whole equation →

    a=2a = 2a=2, b=−9b = -9b=−9, c=5c = 5c=5.

  3. 3

    D=(−9)2−4(2)(5)=81−40=41D = (-9)^2 - 4(2)(5) = 81 - 40 = 41D=(−9)2−4(2)(5)=81−40=41.

  4. 4

    41 is not a perfect square, so D=41\sqrt{D} = \sqrt{41}D​=41​.

  5. 5

    Formula; −b=+9-b = +9−b=+9, 2a=42a = 42a=4.

    x=9±414x = \dfrac{9 \pm \sqrt{41}}{4}x=49±41​​Swipe to see the whole equation →

  6. Check: sum of roots =184=92=−ba= \dfrac{18}{4} = \dfrac{9}{2} = -\dfrac{b}{a}=418​=29​=−ab​ ✔; product =81−4116=4016=52=ca= \dfrac{81 - 41}{16} = \dfrac{40}{16} = \dfrac{5}{2} = \dfrac{c}{a}=1681−41​=1640​=25​=ac​ ✔.

  7. Answer x=9+414 or x=9−414x = \dfrac{9 + \sqrt{41}}{4} \text{ or } x = \dfrac{9 - \sqrt{41}}{4}x=49+41​​ or x=49−41​​

    Common trap: Taking b=9b = 9b=9 (not moving 9x9x9x across), which gives −9±414\dfrac{-9 \pm \sqrt{41}}{4}4−9±41​​ — both roots with the wrong sign.

P13●● StandardShort answer · 3 marksOriginal

Find the values of kkk for which (k+4)x2+(k+1)x+1=0(k + 4)x^2 + (k + 1)x + 1 = 0(k+4)x2+(k+1)x+1=0 has two equal roots. Find the roots for each value.

Full solution

Given: a=k+4a = k + 4a=k+4, b=k+1b = k + 1b=k+1, c=1c = 1c=1. Asked: kkk, and the roots.

Concept used: equal roots ⇔ D=0D = 0D=0; check a≠0a \neq 0a=0 (Topic 5). Why it applies: aaa contains kkk, so the check matters.

  1. 1

    D=(k+1)2−4(k+4)(1)=0D = (k + 1)^2 - 4(k + 4)(1) = 0D=(k+1)2−4(k+4)(1)=0.

  2. 2

    Expand.

    k2+2k+1−4k−16=0k^2 + 2k + 1 - 4k - 16 = 0k2+2k+1−4k−16=0Swipe to see the whole equation →
  3. 3

    Simplify.

    k2−2k−15=0k^2 - 2k - 15 = 0k2−2k−15=0Swipe to see the whole equation →
  4. 4

    Factorise.

    (k−5)(k+3)=0(k - 5)(k + 3) = 0(k−5)(k+3)=0Swipe to see the whole equation →
  5. 5

    So k=5k = 5k=5 or k=−3k = -3k=−3.

  6. 6

    Check aaa: k=5k = 5k=5 → a=9≠0a = 9 \neq 0a=9=0 ✔; k=−3k = -3k=−3 → a=1≠0a = 1 \neq 0a=1=0 ✔. Both are valid.

  7. 7

    k=5k = 5k=5: 9x2+6x+1=09x^2 + 6x + 1 = 09x2+6x+1=0, root x=−618=−13x = -\dfrac{6}{18} = -\dfrac{1}{3}x=−186​=−31​ (twice).

  8. 8

    k=−3k = -3k=−3: x2−2x+1=0x^2 - 2x + 1 = 0x2−2x+1=0, root x=22=1x = \dfrac{2}{2} = 1x=22​=1 (twice).

The product of Tara's age 5 years ago and her age 8 years from now is 30. Find her present age.

Full solution

Given: (age − 5)(age + 8) = 30. Asked: present age.

Concept used: word-problem routine (Topic 6). Why it applies: a product of two expressions in the same unknown.

  1. 1

    Let Tara's present age be xxx years.

  2. 2

    Equation:

    (x−5)(x+8)=30(x - 5)(x + 8) = 30(x−5)(x+8)=30Swipe to see the whole equation →
  3. 3

    Expand.

    x2+3x−40=30x^2 + 3x - 40 = 30x2+3x−40=30Swipe to see the whole equation →
  4. 4

    Subtract 30.

    x2+3x−70=0x^2 + 3x - 70 = 0x2+3x−70=0Swipe to see the whole equation →
  5. 5

    Product −70-70−70, sum 3 → 101010 and −7-7−7.

    (x+10)(x−7)=0(x + 10)(x - 7) = 0(x+10)(x−7)=0Swipe to see the whole equation →
  6. 6

    So x=7x = 7x=7 or x=−10x = -10x=−10.

  7. 7

    Reject x=−10x = -10x=−10: an age cannot be negative. (Also x=7x = 7x=7 gives x−5=2>0x - 5 = 2 > 0x−5=2>0 ✔.)

  8. Check: 2×15=302 \times 15 = 302×15=30 ✔.

  9. Answer Tara is 7 years old.

P20●● StandardLong answer · 5 marksOriginal

A motorboat goes 24 km upstream and returns to its starting point in a total of 5 hours. The speed of the stream is 2 km/h. Find the speed of the boat in still water.

Full solution

Given: 24 km each way; total time 5 h; stream 2 km/h. Asked: boat's speed in still water.

Concept used: upstream speed =x−2= x - 2=x−2, downstream speed =x+2= x + 2=x+2; time =distancespeed= \dfrac{\text{distance}}{\text{speed}}=speeddistance​ (Topic 6). Why it applies: the two times add to 5 h.

  1. 1

    Let the speed of the boat in still water be xxx km/h (x>2x > 2x>2).

  2. 2

    Upstream speed =(x−2)= (x - 2)=(x−2) km/h; downstream speed =(x+2)= (x + 2)=(x+2) km/h.

  3. 3

    Equation: time up + time down =5= 5=5.

    24x−2+24x+2=5\dfrac{24}{x - 2} + \dfrac{24}{x + 2} = 5x−224​+x+224​=5Swipe to see the whole equation →
  4. 4

    Combine over (x−2)(x+2)=x2−4(x - 2)(x + 2) = x^2 - 4(x−2)(x+2)=x2−4.

    24(x+2)+24(x−2)x2−4=5\dfrac{24(x + 2) + 24(x - 2)}{x^2 - 4} = 5x2−424(x+2)+24(x−2)​=5Swipe to see the whole equation →
  5. 5

    Simplify the top: 24x+48+24x−48=48x24x + 48 + 24x - 48 = 48x24x+48+24x−48=48x.

    48xx2−4=5\dfrac{48x}{x^2 - 4} = 5x2−448x​=5Swipe to see the whole equation →
  6. 6

    Multiply both sides by x2−4x^2 - 4x2−4.

    48x=5x2−2048x = 5x^2 - 2048x=5x2−20Swipe to see the whole equation →
  7. 7

    Standard form.

    5x2−48x−20=05x^2 - 48x - 20 = 05x2−48x−20=0Swipe to see the whole equation →
  8. 8

    D=(−48)2−4(5)(−20)=2304+400=2704D = (-48)^2 - 4(5)(-20) = 2304 + 400 = 2704D=(−48)2−4(5)(−20)=2304+400=2704, and 2704=52\sqrt{2704} = 522704​=52.

  9. 9

    Formula.

    x=48±5210x = \dfrac{48 \pm 52}{10}x=1048±52​Swipe to see the whole equation →
  10. 10

    So x=10x = 10x=10 or x=−25x = -\dfrac{2}{5}x=−52​.

  11. 11

    Reject x=−25x = -\dfrac{2}{5}x=−52​: a speed cannot be negative (and it must be more than 2 km/h to go upstream).

  12. Check: upstream 248=3\dfrac{24}{8} = 3824​=3 h, downstream 2412=2\dfrac{24}{12} = 21224​=2 h, total 5 h ✔.

  13. Answer The speed of the boat in still water is 10 km/h.

    Common trap: Using x+2x + 2x+2 for upstream. Going against the stream slows the boat: upstream =x−2= x - 2=x−2.

  4. 4

    Expand.

    2400−100x+x2=21092400 - 100x + x^2 = 21092400−100x+x2=2109Swipe to see the whole equation →

    Standard form.

    So x=3x = 3x=3 or x=97x = 97x=97.

P25●●● AdvancedCase/source-based · 4 marksOriginal

Case: The kitchen garden by the wall

A housing society wants a rectangular kitchen garden against the long boundary wall. The wall forms one side, so fencing is needed only on the other three sides. The gardener has 40 m of fencing and wants an area of 192 m². Let the two sides perpendicular to the wall each be xxx m long.

(a) Show that x2−20x+96=0x^2 - 20x + 96 = 0x2−20x+96=0. (1)
(b) Find the discriminant and state the nature of the roots. (1)
(c) Find both possible sets of dimensions. Which one should be chosen if the side along the wall must be at least 20 m? (2)

OR
(c) Could the same 40 m of fencing enclose an area of 210 m²? Justify. (2)

Full solution

Given: 40 m of fencing on three sides; area 192 m². Asked: parts (a)–(c).

Concept used: modelling with a quadratic, discriminant, and choosing roots that fit (Topic 5, Topic 6). Why it applies: the side along the wall is 40−2x40 - 2x40−2x, so the area is a quadratic in xxx.

  1. 1

    (a)

    Two sides of xxx m use 2x2x2x m of fencing, so the side along the wall is (40−2x)(40 - 2x)(40−2x) m.

  2. 2

    Area: x(40−2x)=192x(40 - 2x) = 192x(40−2x)=192.

  3. 3

    Expand: 40x−2x2=19240x - 2x^2 = 19240x−2x2=192.

  4. 4

P26●●● AdvancedCase/source-based · 4 marksOriginal

Case: The delivery van

A delivery van drives 180 km from a warehouse to a town at a uniform speed of xxx km/h. On the way back, empty and lighter, it travels 10 km/h faster and takes 36 minutes less.

(a) Write the time taken for each journey in terms of xxx. (1)
(b) Form the equation and write it in standard form. (1)
(c) Find the speed of the van on each journey. (2)

Full solution

Given: 180 km each way; return speed x+10x + 10x+10; return 36 minutes shorter. Asked: parts (a)–(c).

Concept used: time =distancespeed= \dfrac{\text{distance}}{\text{speed}}=speeddistance​; convert minutes to hours (Topic 6). Why it applies: the difference of the two times is 3660=35\dfrac{36}{60} = \dfrac{3}{5}6036​=53​ h.

  1. 1

    (a)

    Outward: 180x\dfrac{180}{x}x180​ h. Return: 180x+10\dfrac{180}{x + 10}x+10180​ h.

  2. 2

    (b)

    36 minutes =3660= \dfrac{36}{60}=6036​ h =35= \dfrac{3}{5}=53​ h.

    180x−180x+10=35\dfrac{180}{x} - \dfrac{180}{x + 10} = \dfrac{3}{5}x180​−x+10180​=53​Swipe to see the whole equation →
  3. 3

    Combine: 1800x(x+10)=35\dfrac{1800}{x(x + 10)} = \dfrac{3}{5}x(x+10)1800​=53​.

  4. 4

    Cross-multiply: 9000=3x(x+10)9000 = 3x(x + 10)9000=3x(x+10), so x2+10x=3000x^2 + 10x = 3000x2+10x=3000.

  5. 5

    Standard form: x2+10x−3000=0x^2 + 10x - 3000 = 0x2+10x−3000=0.

  6. 6

    (c)

    Product −3000-3000−3000, sum 10 → 606060 and −50-50−50: (x+60)(x−50)=0(x + 60)(x - 50) = 0(x+60)(x−50)=0.

  7. 7

    Reject x=−60x = -60x=−60 (speed). So x=50x = 50x=50; return speed =60= 60=60 km/h.

  8. Check: 18050=3.6\dfrac{180}{50} = 3.650180​=3.6 h and 18060=3\dfrac{180}{60} = 360180​=3 h; difference 0.60.60.6 h =36= 36=36 min ✔.

  9. Answer (a) 180x\dfrac{180}{x}x180​ h and 180x+10\dfrac{180}{x + 10}x+10180​ h (b) x2+10x−3000=0x^2 + 10x - 3000 = 0x2+10x−3000=0 (c) 50 km/h going, 60 km/h returning.

    Common trap: Using 36 instead of 35\dfrac{3}{5}53​ on the right side; the speeds come out absurdly small.

  5. 5

    x=5±76x = \dfrac{5 \pm 7}{6}x=65±7​.

  8. Answer Errors: (1) ccc should be −2-2−2 (standard form first), (2) −b-b−b should be +5+5+5. Correct roots: x=2 or x=−13x = 2 \text{ or } x = -\dfrac{1}{3}x=2 or x=−31​.

    D=(k−3)2−4(1)(−k)D = (k - 3)^2 - 4(1)(-k)D=(k−3)2−4(1)(−k).

Two pipes running together can fill a water tank in 31133\dfrac{1}{13}3131​ hours. The larger pipe alone takes 3 hours less than the smaller pipe alone. Find the time each pipe takes on its own.

Full solution

Given: together 3113=40133\dfrac{1}{13} = \dfrac{40}{13}3131​=1340​ h; larger pipe 3 h faster. Asked: each pipe's time.

Concept used: rates add: 1x+1x−3=1340\dfrac{1}{x} + \dfrac{1}{x - 3} = \dfrac{13}{40}x1​+x−31​=4013​ (wrap-up, Topic 6). Why it applies: together they fill 1340\dfrac{13}{40}4013​ of the tank per hour.

    Let the smaller pipe take xxx hours. The larger takes (x−3)(x - 3)(x−3) hours.

  2. 2

    Equation:

    1x+1x−3=1340\dfrac{1}{x} + \dfrac{1}{x - 3} = \dfrac{13}{40}x1​+x−31​=4013​Swipe to see the whole equation →
  3. 3

    Combine the left side.

    2x−3x(x−3)=1340\dfrac{2x - 3}{x(x - 3)} = \dfrac{13}{40}x(x−3)2x−3​=4013​Swipe to see the whole equation →
  4. 4

    Cross-multiply.

    40(2x−3)=13x(x−3)40(2x - 3) = 13x(x - 3)40(2x−3)=13x(x−3)Swipe to see the whole equation →
  5. 5

    Expand.

    80x−120=13x2−39x80x - 120 = 13x^2 - 39x80x−120=13x2−39xSwipe to see the whole equation →
  6. 6

    Standard form.

    13x2−119x+120=013x^2 - 119x + 120 = 013x2−119x+120=0Swipe to see the whole equation →
  7. 7

    D=(−119)2−4(13)(120)=14161−6240=7921D = (-119)^2 - 4(13)(120) = 14161 - 6240 = 7921D=(−119)2−4(13)(120)=14161−6240=7921; 7921=89\sqrt{7921} = 897921​=89.

  8. 8

    x=119±8926x = \dfrac{119 \pm 89}{26}x=26119±89​, so x=20826=8x = \dfrac{208}{26} = 8x=26208​=8 or x=3026=1513x = \dfrac{30}{26} = \dfrac{15}{13}x=2630​=1315​.

  9. 9

    Reject x=1513x = \dfrac{15}{13}x=1315​: the larger pipe would take 1513−3<0\dfrac{15}{13} - 3 < 01315​−3<0 hours.

  10. Check: 18+15=5+840=1340\dfrac{1}{8} + \dfrac{1}{5} = \dfrac{5 + 8}{40} = \dfrac{13}{40}81​+51​=405+8​=4013​ ✔.

  11. Answer The smaller pipe takes 8 hours and the larger pipe 5 hours.

    Second equation: x2−2x+k=0x^2 - 2x + k = 0x2−2x+k=0.

    4−4k=04 - 4k = 04−4k=0, so k=1k = 1k=1.

E7 (Exemplar Ex 4.2, Q1 (v))●● StandardShort answer · 2 marksNCERT Exemplar Ch 4, Ex 4.2 Q1 (v)

State whether the following quadratic equation has two distinct real roots. Justify your answer.
(x+4)2−8x=0(x + 4)^2 - 8x = 0(x+4)2−8x=0

Full solution

Given: an equation not in standard form. Asked: whether it has two distinct real roots, with reason.

Concept used: standard form, then DDD (Topic 1, Topic 5). Why it applies: DDD can only be found from standard form.

  1. 1

    Expand: x2+8x+16−8x=0x^2 + 8x + 16 - 8x = 0x2+8x+16−8x=0.

  2. 2

    Simplify: x2+16=0x^2 + 16 = 0x2+16=0, so a=1a = 1a=1, b=0b = 0b=0, c=16c = 16c=16.

  3. 3

    D=0−4(1)(16)=−64<0D = 0 - 4(1)(16) = -64 < 0D=0−4(1)(16)=−64<0.

  4. Check: x2+16≥16x^2 + 16 \geq 16x2+16≥16 for all real xxx, so it is never 0 ✔.

  5. Answer No. It simplifies to x2+16=0x^2 + 16 = 0x2+16=0, whose discriminant is −64<0-64 < 0−64<0, so it has no real roots.

    Common trap: Taking b=8b = 8b=8 from the original form. The 8x8x8x terms cancel.

E8 (Exemplar Ex 4.2, Q2 (v))●● StandardTrue/False with justification · 2 marksNCERT Exemplar Ch 4, Ex 4.2 Q2 (v)

Write whether the following statement is true or false. Justify your answer.
If the coefficient of x2x^2x2 and the constant term of a quadratic equation have opposite signs, then the quadratic equation has real roots.

Full solution

Given: aaa and ccc have opposite signs. Asked: true or false, with reason.

Concept used: D=b2−4acD = b^2 - 4acD=b2−4ac (Topic 5). Why it applies: the signs of aaa and ccc decide the sign of −4ac-4ac−4ac.

  1. 1

    aaa and ccc have opposite signs, so ac<0ac < 0ac<0.

  2. 2

    Then −4ac>0-4ac > 0−4ac>0.

  3. 3

    b2≥0b^2 \geq 0b2≥0 always, so D=b2−4ac>0D = b^2 - 4ac > 0D=b2−4ac>0.

  4. Check: example x2−9=0x^2 - 9 = 0x2−9=0 (a=1a = 1a=1, c=−9c = -9c=−9): roots ±3\pm 3±3 ✔.

  5. Answer True, because ac<0ac < 0ac<0 makes −4ac>0-4ac > 0−4ac>0, so D=b2−4ac>0D = b^2 - 4ac > 0D=b2−4ac>0 and the roots are real (in fact distinct).

  2. 2

    x=−5±132(−3)=−5±13−6x = \dfrac{-5 \pm 13}{2(-3)} = \dfrac{-5 \pm 13}{-6}x=2(−3)−5±13​=−6−5±13​.

    +++ sign: 8−6=−43\dfrac{8}{-6} = -\dfrac{4}{3}−68​=−34​.

E12●● StandardLong answer · 5 marksNCERT Exemplar Ch 4, Ex 4.4 Q4

A train, travelling at a uniform speed for 360 km, would have taken 48 minutes less to travel the same distance if its speed were 5 km/h more. Find the original speed of the train.

Full solution

Given: 360 km; 5 km/h faster → 48 min less. Asked: original speed.

Concept used: time =distancespeed= \dfrac{\text{distance}}{\text{speed}}=speeddistance​; 48 min =45= \dfrac{4}{5}=54​ h (Topic 6). Why it applies: the two times differ by 45\dfrac{4}{5}54​ h.

  1. 1

    Let the original speed be xxx km/h.

  2. 2

    Equation:

    360x−360x+5=45\dfrac{360}{x} - \dfrac{360}{x + 5} = \dfrac{4}{5}x360​−x+5360​=54​Swipe to see the whole equation →
  3. 3

    Combine: 1800x(x+5)=45\dfrac{1800}{x(x + 5)} = \dfrac{4}{5}x(x+5)1800​=54​.

  4. 4

    Cross-multiply: 9000=4x(x+5)9000 = 4x(x + 5)9000=4x(x+5), so x2+5x=2250x^2 + 5x = 2250x2+5x=2250.

  5. 5

    Standard form: x2+5x−2250=0x^2 + 5x - 2250 = 0x2+5x−2250=0.

  6. 6

    Product −2250-2250−2250, sum 5 → 505050 and −45-45−45: (x+50)(x−45)=0(x + 50)(x - 45) = 0(x+50)(x−45)=0.

  7. 7

    Reject x=−50x = -50x=−50 (speed). So x=45x = 45x=45.

  8. Check: 36045=8\dfrac{360}{45} = 845360​=8 h and 36050=7.2\dfrac{360}{50} = 7.250360​=7.2 h; difference 0.80.80.8 h =48= 48=48 min ✔.

  9. Answer The original speed of the train is 45 km/h.

    Common trap: Writing 48 instead of 4860=45\dfrac{48}{60} = \dfrac{4}{5}6048​=54​.
